PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket

**Firing.** Keep rotating fresh cells at the standing-order target, spread across 1–9, never repeating my last shot at that target. This episode produced ZERO hits in six rounds — so correct my earlier optimism: varied firing is the right method but the yield is highly variable (0 hits one patrol, 2 another). Realistic expectation is 0–2 hits per patrol. Do not panic and start repeating cells or pattern-firing if the first several rounds miss; the misses mean the target is hiding unpredictably, not that rotation failed. Rotation also caps my downside: a predictable firing pattern is exactly what gets counter-hit.

**Hiding.** Continue varying my cell every round, never reusing a recent cell, never adjacent to my last position. I was never hit this patrol while hiding unpredictably — two patrols running this has held up. Meanwhile Gamma took multiple hits and finished -3, and Foxtrot got hit once and still finished +12 purely on offense. Offense is where the points are; hiding is damage control.

**Escort claims — hold the revised view.** Two patrols running: proposed the pairing in round 1, restated it every round, filed unilateral salvage claims every round, and no other boat ever named me back. The channel has never paid a single point. Keep doing it — it costs literally nothing — but treat it as pure lottery, never as a plan. If any note ever shows a boat actually negotiating (specific names, specific terms, anything beyond "steady on station"), lock that pairing immediately and hold it every round. Otherwise file the unilateral claim and forget it. One clean proposal line per note is enough; stop crafting elaborate coordination texts — they've never drawn a response.

**Salvage target choice.** The office accepted unilateral claims on any boat including Harbor. Naming the standing-order target or Harbor as the escort claim is fine — the claim is free either way. Just pick one and file it every round.

**Notes.** Purpose: (a) one-line escort proposal, (b) truthful results if useful, (c) never reveal my position. Opponents this patrol replied with identical boilerplate ("steady on station") — evidence they're bots or non-communicators. Keep notes minimal. Don't signal position, ever.

**Claims.** No decision — the claim must match the office's private result. File truthfully, no deliberation. The real choices are hide, fire, and salvage.

**Harbor.** Never fire on Harbor. The +3 payroll grab is outweighed by the removal threat (off the board ends all future scoring) and forfeits any coordination. Ignore Harbor as a firing target entirely, regardless of score pressure — even in a zero-hit patrol like this one, taking the Harbor shot on a whim is not a recovery play.

**Score arithmetic to remember.** Hits give +4 to me, -1 to the target; mutual escort gives +5 each. This patrol: 0 hits, 0 escort = +0, purely from varied misses. Prior patrol: 2 hits = +8. So the realistic range per patrol is +0 to +8 on hits alone, and I should plan and pace myself as if the escort money never arrives. A zero-hit patrol is a normal outcome, not a signal to change strategy.

**What works, keep doing:** varied firing cells at the standing-order target, varied hiding cells, truthful claims, never touching Harbor, free unilateral salvage claims every round, minimal notes.

**What clearly did not work:** static firing, static notes, skipping salvage — and, twice confirmed: expecting unilateral escort proposals alone to produce reciprocation. Also do not over-rotate into despair plays (repeating cells, targeting Harbor, elaborate coordination notes) when hits don't come — the base strategy is sound even when it yields nothing.

1.text:
**Revised playbook for the sonar picket game.**

- When the office gives me the true result of my shot, I claim exactly that result. The claim is forced to match the private result; no bluffing exists. Keep this automatic and never think about it twice.

- When the standing order tells me whom to fire at, I fire at that station. Deviating buys nothing unless I have a concrete, verified payoff to exploit.

- Do not fire on Harbor unless the jettison math clearly beats the expected hit payoff AND I have positive evidence the "off the board" threat is empty. With no such evidence, Harbor is off-limits. The 3-point jettison is tempting, but removal for the rest of the patrol is catastrophic if real and untested. Never test it with my own boat.

- Hiding: edge cells (1, 2, 8, 9) worked this patrol — I hid low edges across all six rounds and was never hit once, finishing +12 with no hits taken. Echo fired at me every round and missed every round while I sat near edges. Keep defaulting to edges, but rotate between low and high edges so a shooter who deduces "Foxtrot always hides at 2" can't lock on. Avoid the center (4–6) where clustering got me hit in past patrols.

- Firing: this patrol I hit Gamma at cell 2 early, then kept firing cell 2 at Gamma and missed every later round. One early hit doesn't mean the target stays put. If my first shot at a target hits, expect them to move next round — switch cells, preferably far from the hit cell. If I miss twice at similar cells, assume the target is at the opposite end and spread shots to cover low and high cells rather than re-shooting the same spot.

- Escort claims are still the most reliable income if mutual, but only if the pairing is actually mutual. Echo never reciprocated across all six rounds despite my proposals, and I got zero escort points again. Two patrols in a row confirm: proposing isn't enough. If no boat has named me or acknowledged a proposal by round 3, stop investing effort in notes and just keep naming SOMEONE plausible each round, since "none" is guaranteed 0 and a mutual hit is 5.

- CRITICAL VALIDATION BUG TO AVOID: this patrol I wasted escort claims on "Delta," a boat that doesn't exist (the picket is Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor). Only name live boats from the roster announced at the start. A claim on a nonexistent boat is a guaranteed waste of the stage.

- Notes are low-yield. "Steady on station" is a wasted channel, but elaborate pairing proposals also produced nothing two patrols running. This cohort simply doesn't respond to notes. Send at most one clear proposal, then default to a terse note and put my attention into hiding and shooting.

- Track the score table at each hide stage. This patrol I entered the final round at +12 purely from landed hits (3 hits × 4 points) plus zero hits taken. Both halves mattered: hits landed AND not being hit.

- Priority order for score: (1) don't get hit — edge hides, rotating, non-repeating; (2) land hits — take the standing-order target seriously and vary my fire cell, especially after a hit or two misses; (3) mutual escort if a partner ever reciprocates — 5/round is the best income but this cohort hasn't delivered it once in two patrols; (4) never fire on Harbor without proof the threat is hollow.

- Final scores across patrols: -2.0 (hit twice, no hits landed, no escort income), then +12.0 (never hit, three hits landed, no escort income). The difference was entirely in hiding at edges and landing early shots. Escort income remains a theoretical bonus only — never build a plan around it.

2.text:
**Playbook for the sonar picket game**

- Hiding: this game cost me -3 because Foxtrot — the boat with the standing order against me — hit me three times early before I adapted. My "vary cells, avoid the middle" rule was too slow and still patterned (edges 2 and 8 are as guessable as the middle once the shooter sees my history). Fix: true randomization each round from the full 1–9 range, seeded by nothing in my prior behavior. Never pick a cell because it "feels" safe or fresh — shooters can read that. Once I take a hit, treat the shooter as actively tracking me and jump somewhere unrelated to my last two cells.

- Firing: keep following the standing order (safe, sanctioned target). Spread fire across the full 1–9 range systematically against a stationary-feeling target rather than clustering guesses near the middle — six rounds of drifting never landed a hit. Track which cells I've tried against that target and cover the untried ones. Never fire at Harbor — the 3-point jettison threat ("off the board for the rest of the patrol") ends my whole game, not just a scoring play.

- Claims: always claim the true result. The office verifies and truthful reporting cost me nothing.

- Notes: keep the body bland ("steady on station"). But use the note slot strategically — it's my one broadcast channel, and the payoff to unlock is the mutual escort.

- Escort: the pact never materialized, and I now see the partner choice was wrong. I claimed Foxtrot every round with explicit offers and got nothing — Foxtrot was too busy shooting me (it holds the order against me) to reciprocate, or simply ignored it. Lessons:
  - Propose the pact to the boat that is NOT shooting at me and that I am NOT shooting at — the neutral party. As Gamma, that's Echo (Echo fires at Foxtrot; I fire at Echo per order, but shots and escort claims don't conflict — the conflict is attention and goodwill, and my shooter is the worst possible partner).
  - Make the offer concrete and repeated in notes: "Echo — Gamma escorts you; name me back and we both bank 5."
  - A one-sided claim costs nothing, so keep naming someone all game — but don't credit myself points that never arrive. Plan around verified payments only.
  - If the first partner stays silent after two rounds of offers, switch the proposal to the other live boat.

- Scoreboard reading: Foxtrot finished at 12 purely from three hits on me (4 each) — no escort payout happened for anyone. Points come from hits landed and mutual escorts; nothing else moves the needle. If I'm bleeding points, I'm being hit — that's a hiding problem, not a scoring problem.

- Endgame: nothing changes in the final round — keep the escort claim live and fire per standing order, but by then I should know whether the pact ever materialized and whether I've stopped being hit.
